mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is causally linked to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce the discount rate for equity valuations.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.2% over the past month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-constrained regime (INDPRO growth < 1.5% annually), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO growth is below 1.5% annually, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases when INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises above 2.5% annually, it signals the Federal Reserve will tighten policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 2.5% annually.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market (PAYEMS) is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as robust employment growth supports consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between PAYEMS and 60-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market recovery regime (HOUST growth > 1.0% annually), a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST growth is above 1.0% annually, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases when HOUST rises.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and labor market strength (PAYEMS) signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining INDPRO and PAYEMS fails to produce negative 5-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases.
